messages.author: 869c96bbc2bac5ee
messages.subject: Problems with plotting
parts:
Dear Wallace team, 
I have been able to run my models with corine land cover and srtm elevation data. 
However, in the Visualization/Map Prediction section, Wallace collapses when I click on "plot". The warning message says: "Raster image too large;  33036699  bytes is greater than maximum 4194304 bytes". Do you have any advice as to what I could do to successfully draw the map? If you need any more info, please let me know. 
Best regards, 
Beni

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Problems with plotting
parts: This is probably an issue with the computer machine's memory or RAM- the landcover and elevation data are probably very high resolution. You might need another form of GIS to visualize as Wallace and the leaflet package seem to be unable to load files this big.

messages.author: 39d5a48204524e3c
messages.subject: Re: Problems with plotting
parts: I've had the same warning message when working with global rasters. When investigating further I noticed that the addRasterImage function can be set to allow for larger than 4MB images with the maxBytes argument. So support for larger images seems to be feasible at least.
